title: Lecture 15 · DNA and the transmission of information

blocks.html:
What to know

  • Nucleotides have a base, sugar, and phosphate. DNA uses deoxyribose and the bases A, T, C, G; RNA uses ribose and uracil instead of thymine.
  • The double helix is antiparallel. A pairs with T (two hydrogen bonds); C pairs with G (three). The sequence is read 5′ to 3′.
  • Replication is semiconservative. Helicase unwinds, DNA polymerase adds nucleotides to a primer, and each daughter duplex keeps one parental strand.
  • Mutations change sequence. Substitutions, insertions, and deletions can be silent, missense, or nonsense; trinucleotide repeats cause several inherited disorders.
  • Inheritance follows patterns. Autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, X-linked, and mitochondrial inheritance each produce characteristic family histories.

Check

check.question: Which base pairs with guanine in DNA?
check.explanation: Guanine pairs with cytosine through three hydrogen bonds; adenine pairs with thymine through two.
